arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 23: aphids on Moshe, 'Wednesday I inspect him, and we talk'; later an iced lemonade at Cafe Nahat after Gadi's call. Tue Nov 24 night: she phones and asks him to come at one tomorrow, she wants to tell him something herself, not on the phone. Next: midpoint Wed Nov 25, Lior lets it slip before she can.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 23: 'Yes, and after Thursday' at lunch, then at 22:49 Gadi phoned again and Ishai made the blue-and-silver banner in ten minutes anyway, free. Tue Nov 24: Gadi's email 'Thursday payment run confirmed!!' with a P.S.: the bank is 'slow in December'. Next: Thursday; week 3 Gadi asks for January.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 23: Tomer phones: one toothbrush, half the shelves empty; Ishai texts Noa 'Saturday. Dinner. Just us. No plumbers.' Tue Nov 24: she phones back, jokes it off ('are you proposing?'), hears that Tomer talked, and cuts the call when 'S.' rings on the other line. Trivia tonight with Tomer (engine). Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19. Mon Nov 23 'After Thursday' to Gadi, then caved at night for the second banner. Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for: where he first says out loud what he wants.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: back on her feet in the robe, she asks Ishai to help her send Eli an early Hanukkah photo; her chat with Eli shows a heart from August and 'busy mom' from June. She says 'he's very busy' twice. Next: Thu Nov 26 she admits it (four years); week 3 Ishai quietly messages Eli.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Promised to explain the envelope 'after the card game'. Tue Nov 24 he is on the phone at the back the whole lunch, 'Thursday, champion, I swear on the oil'. Next: the telling Thu Nov 26.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Fri: chapter fourteen, the barista and the streets up north. Sun-Tue: no cafe visits. Next: Wed Nov 25 at Cafe Nahat he lets Dana's Haifa slip ('so we'll need a new barista...'); Sun Nov 29 Ishai reads chapter one.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 23: fixed Noa's socket, worried about the empty flat, 'ask her, not me, you're her person'. Tue Nov 24: trivia with Noa and Ishai (engine); Noa knows he talked. Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 23: two talks in the park ('three pigeons on the wire, only two have bread'; 'the cold end of the wood'). Next: Ishai tells him how the Dana talk goes.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: First night Mon Nov 23: Ishai finished first of five, 91 shekels up, a 28-shekel pot off Yossi with jack-nine suited; Boaz let slip Yossi has 'financial troubles'. Tue Nov 24 at Avi's Yossi asks to borrow 200 'till the first', admits the cap has been broke since summer and he owes at the depot; Ishai lends it (his winnings plus 109). Next: second night Mon Dec 7, Yossi pays back in coins.

beats.goal: Back from the lecture, Ishai stops at Avi's kiosk for lunch (Avi is on the phone at the back, busy). Yossi, in his depot work shirt and the lucky cap, has been waiting for him. He jokes about the 'professor' who took his 28 shekels, then, too casually, asks to borrow 200 'till the first'. Ishai remembers Moti's rule ('nobody lends at the table') - this isn't the table. Yossi admits the cap has been broke since summer and he owes at the depot. Ishai lends it: his 91 winnings plus 109. Yossi is ashamed and grateful; asks him not to tell Boaz. Then Gadi's email arrives.
beats.teaser: The man in the lucky cap needs a word with last night's winner.
beats.forceText: At Avi's kiosk Yossi asks Ishai to lend him 200 shekels till the first; Ishai lends it from his poker winnings.

forceLines.say: Two hundred, professor. Till the first. Swear on the cap.
It's not the table. Okay. Two hundred.

forceCommentary.say: He won 91 and lent 200. That's not poker, that's a charity with chips.
Moti's rule was 'nobody lends at the table'. Technically correct. The worst kind.

moments.text: Lunchtime at Avi's kiosk. Avi is on the phone at the back, his back turned. Yossi, in his depot shirt and the lucky cap, leans on the counter as if he's been waiting. He has.

lines.say: Professor! The man who robbed me with jack-nine.
Hi, Yossi. Sorry about that.
Don't be sorry. Be lucky. You were lucky.
I didn't even know it was good.
That's the best way. The cards like the innocent.
Are you eating?
Me? No. Already ate. At the depot.
It's twelve thirty.
Listen. Small thing. Between us.
Okay...
Two hundred. Till the first. Swear on the cap.
Moti said nobody lends at the table.
Is this a table? It's a kiosk. Different rules.
Yossi, is everything okay?
The cap's been on holiday since summer. And the depot... I owe a little.
How much is a little?
More than two hundred. Less than a bus.

commentary.say: 'Already ate at the depot.' At twelve thirty. Nobody eats at a depot. Not even buses.
And Avi's back is turned. The one time he doesn't hand out a proverb.

then.text: Ishai orders a falafel and eats slowly while Yossi looks at the street, the cap pulled low.

moments.text: Ishai takes out the envelope from last night, counts the 91 shekels, then adds his own notes until it is 200. Yossi takes it fast and folds it twice.

lines.say: Ninety-one is yours anyway, really.
No, no. It's yours. You won it.
Then I'm lending you my win. And a bit.
You're a strange gambler, professor.
I'm not a gambler. I'm a designer.
Same thing. You both hope.
I only hope for files that open.
Don't tell Boaz. He drives with me. He'd worry.
I won't tell Boaz.
First of the month. Every shekel.
I know.
In coins, maybe. But every shekel.
Coins are fine. Eat something, Yossi.
Now I'll eat. Now I can.

commentary.say: Yossi just ordered a falafel with Ishai's money. I'm not crying, it's the tahini.
'In coins, maybe.' Ishai will be paid like a parking meter.

update.memory: Borrowed 200 from Ishai at Avi's till the first: his poker win plus his own. Told him the cap's broke since summer, owes at the depot. Don't tell Boaz.

message.say: Banner PERFECT!! Thursday payment run confirmed!! P.S. the bank is a bit slow in December, don't panic if it's Friday.

moments.text: Walking home along Herzl Street, Ishai reads Gadi's email twice on the pavement.

lines.say: 'Don't panic if it's Friday.' Who said anything about panic?
Two hundred out. Thursday in. Maybe Friday. Maybe.

commentary.say: A P.S. about the bank. Gadi's emails have trailers now.
Thursday-ish became Friday-ish. Watch the '-ish' grow, people.

beats.goal: Afternoon walk with Falafel in the park. Noa phones about his text from yesterday ('Saturday. Dinner. Just us. No plumbers.'). She jokes it off ('are you proposing?'), says yes, she'll bring wine. Ishai says Tomer was worried about her flat. A pause; she gets sharp: 'Tomer talks too much.' Ishai doesn't back off (the improv), just says 'Saturday, then.' A call waiting beeps on her side; she reads the name and goes quiet, says she has to take it, 'see you at trivia, don't be wrong about ice ships'. She must not explain who it is. Ishai sits on the bench with it.
beats.teaser: Ishai asked Noa to Saturday dinner. 'Just us.' She calls back.
beats.forceText: Noa phones Ishai in the park: yes to Saturday dinner, but she gets sharp when he mentions Tomer, then hangs up for another call.

forceLines.say: Saturday, fine. But I'm bringing wine, not plumbers.
Tomer was worried about you. That's all.

forceCommentary.say: She took the other call in one second. Who gets that kind of priority?
'Tomer talks too much.' Tomer talks exactly enough. That's the problem.

moments.text: Late afternoon in the park, Falafel sniffing the bench legs. Ishai's phone rings: Noa. He answers before the second ring.

lines.say: 'Saturday. Dinner. Just us. No plumbers.' Ishush. Are you proposing?
No. I'm inviting.
With full stops. Very dramatic.
I wanted it to sound real.
It sounded like a ransom note.
Is that a yes?
Yes. Fine. I'll bring wine, not plumbers.
Good. Noa...
Uh oh. 'Noa, dot dot dot.'
Tomer was worried. About your flat.
...Tomer talks too much.
He fixed your socket. He's allowed to worry.
He's allowed to fix sockets.
Saturday, then. Just us.
Wait, I've got another call—
Who is it?
Nobody. I have to take it. Trivia at seven thirty. Don't be wrong about ice ships.
Noa—

commentary.say: 'Nobody.' Nobody makes you go that quiet, babe.
A ransom note with full stops. Ishai's first threat. Very polite.

then.text: He walks Falafel round the pond once, slowly, phone still in his hand.

update.memory: Said yes to Saturday dinner at Ishai's, just us. He said Tomer was worried about my flat. I said Tomer talks too much and hung up for another call.

moments.text: Ishai sits on the cold end of the bench, Falafel's head on his shoe, looking at the call log: 'Noa, 2 min'.

lines.say: 'Nobody.' Nobody doesn't make you hang up that fast.
Saturday. Just us. Okay, Falafel.

commentary.say: He's sitting on the cold end again. Mr. Zelig would have notes.
Ishai's starting to read people. Saturday just got a lot more interesting.

beats.goal: Coming up with Falafel, Ishai finds Mrs. Levi at her door in her robe, the cough nearly gone, with her phone and a framed photo of her late husband lighting a hanukkiah. She wants to send Eli in Toronto an early Hanukkah photo and the phone 'doesn't listen'. Ishai helps; viewers glimpse the chat: a heart in August, 'busy mom' in June, before that long messages only from her. She says 'he's very busy' twice, brightly. Ishai notices but doesn't ask yet. The photo goes; no reply. She feeds him a slice of honey cake and sends him off to his 'quiz'. She must not admit the four years today.
beats.teaser: Mrs. Levi wants to send Toronto a photo. The phone 'doesn't listen'.
beats.forceText: Ishai helps Mrs. Levi send her son Eli an early Hanukkah photo on her phone; she says he is very busy.

forceLines.say: He's very busy, Eli. Toronto is a busy city.

forceCommentary.say: 'Very busy.' Twice in one minute. Mrs. Levi, we heard you the first time.
Two grey ticks. The loneliest colour in the phone.

moments.text: On the landing Mrs. Levi stands at her door in her flowered robe, phone in one hand, a framed photo of her late husband with a hanukkiah in the other. Her cough is almost gone.

lines.say: Ishai! Motek. The phone doesn't listen to me.
Hi, Mrs. Levi. You sound better.
Better. The cough left. It got bored of me.
What does the phone not do?
This. I want Eli to have this. Early, for Hanukkah.
A photo of the photo? Okay. Hold it still.
My Yitzhak. Every year, the same face at the candles.
He looks proud.
He was proud of the candles. Not of his singing.
Now we open Eli...
There. Top. No, scroll. Don't read.
I'm not reading. I'm just... sending.
He's very busy, Eli. Toronto is a busy city.
Sent. Two grey ticks.
Grey is fine. Grey means he's working.
Sure.
He's very busy.

commentary.say: Heart in August. 'Busy mom' in June. Everything else in that chat is her. I counted.
Ishai said 'sure'. Ishai never says just 'sure'. He saw it.

then.text: She props the framed photo against the door frame and they both look at the phone for a while. Nothing turns blue.

moments.text: Mrs. Levi gives up on the phone, disappears inside and comes back with a thick slice of honey cake on a napkin.

lines.say: Eat. You're going to the quiz, you need sugar for the brain.
Thank you. You don't have to.
I have to. Who else will eat it? The cats are on a diet.
I'll come by tomorrow for Ben-Gurion's breakfast.
He likes you more than me now. Traitor.
He likes the tuna.
Same thing, with cats. With people too.
Mrs. Levi... if you want, I'll check your phone later. For a reply.
He'll answer. When he can. Go, go, be smart.
Did he send photos? Of Toronto?
Snow. Once. A lot of snow. Very busy snow.
Maybe he'll send the candles back.
Maybe. Eat the cake, motek. Then go.
Thank you for the cake.

commentary.say: 'The cats are on a diet.' That's a woman with too much cake and not enough visitors.
He offered to check the phone later. He'll remember. That's the scary part.

update.memory: Ishai helped me send Eli the photo of Yitzhak with the candles. Two grey ticks. I said Eli is busy. He offered to check later. Gave him honey cake.

beats.goal: Home after trivia, Ishai is telling Falafel about the ice-ship question when Dana phones after closing the cafe. She's tired and unusually serious under the deadpan. She asks him to come at one tomorrow, after his lecture: she wants to tell him something herself, in person, 'before someone does it worse'. He asks for a hint; she won't; she says it's not bad, it's big, and she hasn't decided anything. She also asks about Moshe's aphids (soap, water, gently). He promises one o'clock. She must not say Haifa or what it is.
beats.teaser: Dana calls after closing. She wants to tell him something herself.
beats.forceText: Dana phones after closing the cafe and asks Ishai to come at one tomorrow: she wants to tell him something in person.

forceLines.say: One o'clock. I want to tell you myself.

forceCommentary.say: 'Before someone does it worse.' Darling, someone always does it worse. Usually at a cafe.
Moshe's aphids got a follow-up question. Moshe is the only one getting straight answers tonight.

moments.text: Back from trivia, Ishai is telling Falafel about the ice-ship question when the phone lights up: Dana. Behind her, chairs being stacked on tables.

lines.say: Hey. It's me. Did you win?
Hi! Ask Noa. I stopped counting after the ice ship.
Ice ship. I won't ask.
Everyone asks. Then they regret it.
How's Moshe? The guests?
Soap, water, gently. Twice. Fewer guests.
Good. Don't get clever with sprays.
I'm not clever. I'm gentle.
Ishai. Tomorrow. After your lecture. One o'clock, at the cafe?
Sure. Coffee?
Coffee. And I want to tell you something.
Tell me now.
Not on the phone. Myself. Before someone does it worse.
Is it bad?
It's not bad. It's big. I haven't decided anything.
Decided what?
One o'clock, Ishai.
One o'clock.

commentary.say: 'I haven't decided anything.' That's what people say when they're deciding. I'm shipping it anyway.
He made the ice ship sound charming. On the phone. To Dana. Ishai is having a growth spurt.

then.text: After the call he stands by the counter, phone against his chin, looking at Moshe.

update.memory: Called Ishai after closing. Asked him to come at one tomorrow; I want to tell him myself, before someone does it worse. Said it's big, not bad.

moments.text: Ishai checks Moshe's leaves under the kitchen light, one by one. Then he sets an alarm on his phone for 12:45 and labels it.

lines.say: 'Big. Not bad.' Moshe, what's big and not bad?
Alarm: 12:45. 'Don't be late. Don't say sorry.'

commentary.say: He labelled the alarm. Ishai's alarms have more courage than he does.
One o'clock tomorrow. Set your alarms too, people. We'll be there.

hook.text: Dana asks him to come at one tomorrow: 'I want to tell you myself, before someone does it worse.' Will she get there first?

previously.text: Whose emergency? Ishai won poker, 91 shekels up, 28 of them from Yossi. Boaz let slip Yossi has 'financial troubles'. Nobody asked him. Yet.

hosts: Tuesday. Last night Ishai won at poker. He said sorry to his chips.
First of five, 91 shekels up. The quiet one is a shark. A very apologetic shark.
Ronit lost 26 to a man who apologises before he bets. She's taking notes. In red pen.
Moti called every bet and lost a hundred. Moti calls everything. Bets. Meetings. Neighbours.
The lucky cap is still on holiday. Nobody has sent a postcard.
Lecture today: Project Habakkuk. A ship made of ice. Ishai is very excited. Nobody else is.
Ishai finished Gadi's second free banner at eleven last night. 'After Thursday' lasted nine hours.
Moshe's aphids: fewer today. Oren cried a little at the sink update.
Gadi says Thursday. Gadi's Thursdays have the life span of a fruit fly.
Trivia tonight at Cafe Nahat. HERZL HEADS want revenge on THE OWLS.
Last week second place. This week Ishai has a theory about ice ships. God help them.
Noa hasn't answered his 'Saturday' text yet. Noa answers everything in under a minute. Hm.
Tomer saw one toothbrush. He hasn't stopped thinking about it. Neither have we.
Mrs. Levi's cough is nearly gone. Her opinions were never ill.
Falafel slept through the whole poker night. Best poker face in the building.
Thirteen degrees this morning. Tel Aviv calls it winter. The rest of the world calls it spring.
Tomorrow is Wednesday. Dana said 'we talk'. Zohar has been ready since Saturday.
Ishai has two hundred reasons to check his bank app this week.
Avi promised to explain the envelope 'after the card game'. The card game is over, Avi.
Ben-Gurion the cat waits on the landing at nine. Ishai wakes at half past. The cat is not impressed.
Ronit said nothing all night. Teachers who say nothing are planning homework.
Boaz ran poker like a bus route. Started on time. Ended on time. Nobody got off early.
If Ishai wins trivia too, we'll have to call him lucky. He'll apologise for it.
The Ruti draft is still in drafts. It's started paying rent there.
Oren's Moshe report: one new leaf, zero aphids on it. A clean leaf. A sign.
Zohar's Dana report: nothing to report. Zohar is reporting it anyway.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Tuesday morning. Clear skies, thirteen degrees, scarves optional.
Tel Aviv, put a jacket over your shoulders and act surprised at noon.
Traffic on Herzl is light. Unless you're a pigeon. Then it's very heavy.
A listener asks if winter is coming. Listener, winter is a rumour here.
Up next, a song about a sailor who never left the harbour. Relatable.
Quiz tip of the day: if you don't know, say 'the Romans'. Works half the time.
It's lunchtime. If you're still at the desk, the desk has won.
Message to the man who left his umbrella on line 88: it's sunny. You're fine.
Small reminder: Hanukkah in ten days. Start the doughnut training now.
Afternoon on 88.2. The light goes gold at four. Go and look at it.
Tonight: clear and cool, ten degrees by midnight. Socks for everyone.
For the night owls: the moon is up, the buses are slow, the falafel is hot.
Radio Herzl, still here, still on 88.2, still not sure who's listening. Hi.

zelig: The pigeons know who has bread. People never know.
A loan is a story you tell the future.
The duck goes in circles. So does the city. So do I.
Cards in the evening, regrets in the morning. Not always. Sometimes.
michal: Tuesday. Legs day. Every day is legs day.
Run club Friday. Seven sharp. I'll text the group. I'll go. Probably.
Why is the dog guy smiling? Did he win something?
sivan: Incline five today. Monday was a rehearsal.
The slow one is late again. Good. Fewer witnesses.
Speed ten. Don't look at me, treadmill. Just go.
lior: Chapter fifteen. The barista packs one cup. Only one.
Up north the coffee is worse. That's the tragedy.
He told his coffee to have a nice day. I can't make that up. I didn't.
kobi: Tuesday is a quiet beer. A quiet beer is still a beer.
My system says Thursday is lucky. My system says that every week.
Nine o'clock. One more. Then the system.
Who wins at poker on a Monday? Lucky people. And liars.

street: ...so I told him, a kiosk is not a bank...
...the 88 was early. Early! I almost cried...
...she says it's winter, I say it's thirteen degrees...
...no, the other dog, the fluffy one...
market: ...two kilos, but the nice ones, not the ones in front...
...my mother makes it with more cinnamon. Wrong, but more...
park: ...the duck has a name, but he won't say it...
...three laps and then coffee, that's the deal...
...I said I'd call her back. That was Tuesday. Last Tuesday...
...look, the old man is talking to the pigeons again...
cafe: ...trivia tonight, we need someone who knows rivers...
...oat milk, but don't tell my trainer...
...she's been quiet all week, the barista...
...the guy with the laptop always writes the same page...

chat.say: Reminder: building fees by Thursday. Cash to Moti. Receipts. Congratulations to apt 4 on the cards, by the way.
Lost 100 last night. Not discussing it. Fees still due.
Who parked a bicycle in front of the mailboxes? It has a basket and an attitude.
Cough is gone. Thank you all for the soup. Ishai, Ben-Gurion says the tuna was late today.
Next cards night Monday December 7. Bring small notes. Professor, bring your luck.
Does anyone know why the ticks stay grey? Asking for a friend.
Grey means delivered, not read. Blue means read. Sorry Mrs. Levi.
Quiet hours from 23:00. Including washing machines. Especially washing machines.
